Balanced V-fold cross-validation

Source: R/balanced_vfold_cv.R
balanced_vfold_cv.Rd

balanced_vfold_cv() splits the data into v folds of about equal size that are similar on several variables at once. Each fold is used once as the assessment set, and the other folds form the analysis set.

Usage

balanced_vfold_cv(
  data,
  v = 10,
  repeats = 1,
  balance = NULL,
  exact = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  method = "anticlust",
  options = list()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

v

The number of folds.

repeats

The number of times to repeat the V-fold partitioning.

balance

<tidy-select> Columns to balance across the sets. Numeric columns are standardized. Factor, character, and logical columns become one indicator column per level.

exact

<tidy-select> Categorical columns to stratify exactly. Each combination of levels is one stratum. In each stratum, the count in every set is the floor or the ceiling of its proportional share, based on the actual size of that set. For folds, the counts of a stratum also differ by at most one over the folds whenever both rules can hold at once. With group, these counts are numbers of groups, not rows.

group

<tidy-select> One column with group IDs. All rows of a group go to the same set. See Details.

method

The balancing method: "anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", or "interaction". See Details.

options

A named list of options for the method. See Details.

Value

A tibble with class balanced_vfold_cv and rset. It has a splits column of rsplit objects and one or two ID columns.

Methods

  • "anticlust" (default) uses k-plus anticlustering (Papenberg, 2024) with anticlust::fast_anticlustering(). It makes the means and the variances of the sets similar. Options are:

    • moments (default 2): the highest moment to balance. 1 balances means only, 3 adds skewness, and 4 adds kurtosis.

    • covariances (default FALSE): also balance the product of each pair of balance columns.

    • k_neighbours (default Inf): the number of nearest neighbours each row may swap with. Inf tries every swap. A small number, such as 20, is faster on large data.

    • local_maximum (default TRUE): repeat the exchange passes until a pass makes no swap (at most 100 passes). FALSE runs one pass.

    • repetitions (default 1): the number of random starts. The best result is kept.

    The anticlust package is required.

  • "twinning" uses twinning::multiplet() for folds. Options are strategy (1, 2, or 3; strategy 2 needs v to be a power of 2) and leaf_size. For v = 2, strategies 1 and 2 give the same result. Strata with fewer than 2 * v rows are assigned at random. The twinning package is required.

  • "rerandomize" draws stratified random splits and keeps the first one whose Mahalanobis imbalance is under a threshold (Morgan and Rubin, 2012). For folds, the imbalance is the largest over the "one fold versus the rest" comparisons. The threshold is the p_accept quantile of the imbalance over pilot draws made with the same exact and group constraints (max(100, min(10 / p_accept, max_draws)) draws). Draws that tie with the threshold are accepted at random, so that the acceptance rate is close to p_accept even for discrete data. If p_accept is below 1 / max(100, max_draws), the pilot draws can't resolve it, and the threshold is the best pilot draw. Options are p_accept, the target acceptance rate (default 0.1), and max_draws (default 1000). If no draw meets the threshold, the best draw is used with a warning.

  • "interaction" cuts numeric columns into quantile bins, crosses all bins, and stratifies at random. It is a baseline that shows how crossed strata become sparse. Options are n_bins (default 4) and pool (default 0.1): cells with less than this fraction of the rows are pooled.

Groups

If you use group, each group becomes one row before the method runs. This row holds the group means of the standardized balance columns and the log of the group size. The method assigns groups, and then each row gets the set of its group. The number of groups per set follows the target proportions, so the number of rows per set is only approximate. exact columns must be constant within each group.

Use with tune

tune and rsample::reshuffle_rset() find the function that made an rset by its class name. They only find balanced_vfold_cv() when balancesample is attached with library(balancesample). If you call balancesample::balanced_vfold_cv() without attaching the package, tune::fit_resamples() and tune::tune_grid() fail with "Could not find function".

If a workflow has a postprocessor that must be trained, such as a calibration from the tailor package, tune splits each analysis set again. That inner split is a balanced_initial_split() with the same balance, exact, group, method, and options, and with prop = 1 - 1/v.

References

Morgan, K. L., & Rubin, D. B. (2012). Rerandomization to improve covariate balance in experiments. The Annals of Statistics, 40(2), 1263-1282.

Papenberg, M. (2024). K-plus anticlustering: An improved k-means criterion for maximizing between-group similarity. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 77(1), 80-102.

Papenberg, M., & Klau, G. W. (2021). Using anticlustering to partition data sets into equivalent parts. Psychological Methods, 26(2), 161-174.

Vakayil, A., & Joseph, V. R. (2022). Data twinning. Statistical Analysis and Data Mining, 15(5), 598-610.

See also

balanced_initial_split(), balance_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
folds <- balanced_vfold_cv(
  mtcars,
  v = 4,
  balance = c(mpg, hp, wt),
  exact = am,
  method = "rerandomize"
)
folds
#> # 4-fold balanced cross-validation (rerandomize), stratified by am
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   splits         id   
#>   <list>         <chr>
#> 1 <split [24/8]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [24/8]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [24/8]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [24/8]> Fold4
balance_check(folds)
